correctness.rationale: Using paired dual bases on the two transverse Lagrangians (with the appropriate sign adjustment in odd characteristic), the neighbours of X are graphs of symmetric forms. For s=dim(X∩A), the principal block of order m=n−s has nullity dim(Y∩A). Extending the block independently gives the factor q^(N_n−N_m), and its nullity-t choices are [m choose t]_q I_q(m−t) by choosing its radical and a nonsingular quotient form. Similarly choosing X∩A gives the stated stratum sizes. Bordering a symmetric matrix produces a nonsingular extension with probability 1−1/q when the old nullity is zero or one, and zero for higher nullity. The recurrence yields the claimed paired nonsingularity probabilities in all characteristics. In the normalized row difference the ratio of adjacent m-rows is (1−q^(−m))/(1−q^(−(m−t))) times the ratio of nonsingularity probabilities; this gives the stated cancellation of paired columns, also at the endpoint t=m−1. Round two is governed by p(s,0), hence identifies exactly the stated pairs or singletons. For odd n, m is even at the first row of each pair, and equality at column 0, equality at the anchor column, and cancellation on odd-starting column pairs give equitability. For even n≥4, every round-two pair has a nonzero difference at column 1, already its own cell, so round three is both sufficient and necessary. The small n=2,3 cases are already stable after round one. An independent finite check directly counted symmetric matrices for q=2,3 through order four and reproduced the quotient partitions in ranks 2–4; it does not prove the quotient in all ranks. Both frozen checkers and outputs were inspected without running uploaded code.
